Describe the transitions between statuses over time

Source: R/transitions.R
describe_transitions.Rd

A status that follows a unit over time, such as education, labour market attachment or civil status, can only change in some ways: a person who has completed an education cannot later not have started it. The transition table counts, for every pair of statuses, how many units go from the one to the other between two observations. Impossible transitions show as cells that should be empty, before any rule is written; require one with ensure_transitions().

Usage

describe_transitions(data, id, time, status)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, or a database or Arrow table: see Database and Arrow tables in checkpoints.

id

Column(s) identifying the unit (tidy-select), e.g. cpr.

time

The period column, or the start of a spell (one column).

status

The status column (one column).

Value

An object of class inshape_transitions, printed as a summary. It is a list with ids, time, status, the counts n_rows, n_units and n_transitions (pairs of consecutive observations), and transitions, a tibble with from, to, units (units making the transition at least once) and n (times it is made).

Details

Each row is compared with the unit's next observation in time, whatever the distance: a person observed as completed in 2019 and as not started in 2021 makes that transition even if 2020 is missing. Find the missing years with ensure_balanced(). Rows with a missing time or status are left out, as missing is a different problem than a wrong status.

The unit is what the id columns say. A person may complete one education and start another; then the unit is the person and the education, id = c(cpr, education), not the person, or the new start looks like a step back.

The same works for spells: give the start column as time, and each spell is compared with the unit's next spell.

See also

ensure_transitions() to forbid transitions, carry_status() to let a status stand once reached.

Examples

education <- data.frame(
  cpr    = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "c", "c"),
  year   = c(2019, 2020, 2021, 2019, 2020, 2019, 2021),
  status = c("not started", "enrolled", "completed",
             "enrolled", "completed", "completed", "not started")
)
# c goes from completed to not started
describe_transitions(education, cpr, year, status)
#> ── Transitions: status by year per cpr ─────────────────────────────────────────
#> 7 rows, 3 units, 4 pairs of consecutive observations
#> 
#> • Changing status: 4 of 4 pairs (100.0%)
#> 
#> Units per transition, from (rows) to (columns):
#>   from \ to   completed  enrolled  not started
#>   completed            0         0            1
#>   enrolled             2         0            0
#>   not started          0         1            0
